stories.title: At least 1 dead, several injured after van rams into crowd at Pride festival; suspect 'known to police'
bullet_points: A van rammed into the Christopher Street Day festival in Berlin's Tiergarten, killing one person, and police launched an intensive manhunt and later identified a suspect with alleged Islamic ties.

stories.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride vehicle attack is dead, police say
bullet_points: Germany's interior minister Alexander Dobrindt described the incident as a likely "Islamic terror attack," and named the suspect as Abdul Ballout, who was born in Germany and has Lebanese roots.

stories.title: Saudi nuclear deal: What US policy shift means for Mideast diplomacy
bullet_points: Saudi Arabia has long sought a nuclear program to support economic growth.
The United States, seeking to avoid a Mideast nuclear arms race, previously had imposed strict restrictions on sharing nuclear technology in the region.

stories.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC
bullet_points: UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease  A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
Continue reading...

stories.title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds
bullet_points: Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well  One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.

There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve  the global target of zero hunger  by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.
Continue reading...

stories.title: Modi’s greatest challenge yet? Delhi struggles to contain student unrest.
bullet_points: Long-simmering frustrations with corruption and youth unemployment have bubbled over into India’s streets.
And in what is arguably the biggest test yet for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government, India’s young “cockroaches” aren’t backing down.

stories.title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying
bullet_points: The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year  Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.
Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively.
They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.

stories.title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers
bullet_points: September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences  The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.

While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.

stories.title: IOC drops Russia ban, but it might not be all good news for the Kremlin
bullet_points: Russia’s exile from international sports competition might be in the process of ending – though at a potential domestic political cost for Moscow.

stories.title: Flames Advance on Bordeaux, Where Evacuees Balance Dread and Hope
bullet_points: With surrounding towns in southwestern France evacuated and fire still spreading rapidly, several thousand are sheltering in the city, unsure what will become of their homes.

stories.title: The Accidental Hero Who Faced Down India’s Government
bullet_points: Abhijeet Dipke founded the Cockroach Janta Party as a joke after a judge insulted young people.
The idea snowballed into a generational movement that has challenged the country’s leaders.

stories.title: Hamas taps 'ultimate institutional survivor' as terror chief, sending message to Israel: expert
bullet_points: Khalil al-Hayya, whose four sons were killed in Israeli strikes, takes over as Hamas political chief in a move experts say signals continuity over change.

stories.title: Trump likes daily strikes on Iran, Sen. Kennedy says: ‘You have to kill a few chickens to scare the monkeys’
bullet_points: Sen.
John Kennedy (R-LA) claimed Sunday that President Trump likes to conduct daily strikes on Iran as he called for the US to ramp up pressure rather than pause them to allow negotiations to continue.

stories.title: Europe will one day thank Trump for 'shaking' it out of its 'complacency': UK defense chief
bullet_points: Wes Streeting says Europe will ultimately thank President Trump for forcing NATO allies to end their overreliance on the U.S.
for defense and security.

stories.title: Ukraine suffers highest civilian casualties of the war in four years — with kids among latest killed
bullet_points: Ukraine has suffered its highest monthly number of civilian casualties in the last four years of war, according to Kyiv's estimates.

stories.title: Water outage at UK’s Gatwick Airport leaves toilets out of order, restaurants closed
bullet_points: The airport said it was providing bottled water, though some passengers disputed that.

stories.title: Tadej Pogačar of Slovenia wins the 2026 Tour de France, his fifth victory in the race
bullet_points: The route for the iconic cycling race's final stage was shortened because security and police were reassigned to assist with wildfires in southwest France.

stories.title: U.S. pauses attacks on Iran for a second straight day and Tehran does too
bullet_points: The United States paused attacks on Iran for a second straight day Sunday and Tehran said it had done so too, as efforts continued to bring the countries back to negotiations on an interim ceasefire.

stories.title: Tanker hits mine in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran intercepts six vessels
bullet_points: An oil tanker blew up in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine on Sunday, Iran's military-linked state media reported, adding that the Islamic republic has intercepted at least six ships in the past 24 hours.

stories.title: U.S.-Iran War Pauses for 2nd Straight Day With Both Sides Holding Off on Strikes
bullet_points: President Trump put off plans to escalate the fighting in part because of dwindling stockpiles of interceptor missiles, American officials said.

stories.title: Toronto police investigate gunfire, vandalism targeting Jewish-owned bakery chain
bullet_points: Toronto police say gunfire struck one location of a Jewish-owned bakery chain while a second sustained window damage, prompting a hate crime investigation.

stories.title: Breakfasts around the world: Syrnyky, or curd-chees hotcakes in Ukraine
bullet_points: Everyone in Ukraine has a story about syrnyki, the tangy, curd-cheese pancakes that have been a breakfast staple for hundreds of years.

stories.title: Wildfires displace more than 250,000 in France, threaten famed wine region
bullet_points: The Gironde fire has burned 162 square miles as 2,500 firefighters and 1,500 soldiers battle the blaze advancing erratically toward Bordeaux.

stories.title: South Africa’s illegal migration backlash mirrors political battles across the West
bullet_points: Over 160,000 immigrants have fled as the March and March movement goes house-to-house demanding foreigners leave amid 32.7% unemployment rate.

stories.title: Lebanese displaced by war turn to satellites to check their homes
bullet_points: Unable to return home, some Lebanese displaced by Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon are buying satellite images to see whether their houses survived.

stories.title: Unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir casts doubt over polls – and region’s future
bullet_points: In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, protests over political representation reveal a growing divide between locals and Islamabad.

stories.title: Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail
bullet_points: Exclusive: CSI Aviation and GlobalX accused of violating civil rights as part of Trump immigration crackdown  Venezuelan men sent last year to a notorious Salvadorian terrorism prison by the Trump administration are suing the US aviation companies that transported them there.

A  lawsuit  filed this week in federal court in Washington DC accuses the companies CSI Aviation and GlobalX of violating the Venezuelans’ civil rights, false imprisonment, intentional infliction of emotional distress, negligence and other violations, for their role in flying the three planes that took the men to El Salvador.
Continue reading...

stories.title: Brazil’s government denies visas to US officials over upcoming elections
bullet_points: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will bid for reelection against Sen.
Flávio Bolsonaro, whose family has many ties with the Trump administration.

stories.title: North Carolina physical therapist disappears in the Caribbean as husband pleads for ‘safe return’
bullet_points: A North Carolina woman vanished while visiting the Caribbean island nation of Grenada as her husband pleaded for "nothing less than her safe return."

stories.title: Trump Says Colombia Will Accept Deportees, Ending Tariff Standoff

bullet_points: In France, around 50,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight into Sunday, according to interior minister Laurent Nuñez.
At least one person has died in a fire in Spain, officials said .

stories.title: FBI ‘Most Wanted’ fraud suspect arrested in Jamaica over alleged $32M COVID-19 relief scheme
bullet_points: Elaine Angene Escoe, 41, arrived back in South Florida Thursday after Jamaican authorities arrested her following a federal manhunt.

stories.title: Ukraine drone strikes on Wildberries warehouses hit Russian sellers, consumers
bullet_points: Ukraine's attacks on warehouses of the Russian online retailer Wildberries have hurt small businesses and some consumers.

stories.title: Pirlo out of Italy football top job after backlash over Russian betting firm links

stories.title: Moment Ukrainian drones strike Russia’s Belgorod

stories.title: US deports Kenyan former NFL player Daniel Adongo

stories.title: Oil price dives as US and Iran pause attacks

bullet_points: Mamdani walked back his threat last week, acknowledging he lacked the legal power to arrest Netanyahu on a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court.

stories.title: Sam Altman says AI has entered ‘singularity’: Should we be worried?
bullet_points: The 'singularity' refers to the point at which AI outpaces human intelligence and becomes difficult to control.

stories.title: The Ban: A censorship loophole during the conflict in Northern Ireland
bullet_points: A censorship saga about how the voices of republican leaders in Northern Ireland were banned by the British government.

stories.title: Cuba, Lacking Fuel, Relies on Ingenuity to Defy Trump’s Blockade
bullet_points: President Trump has tried to strangle Cuba by blocking its oil imports.

stories.title: Ukrainian Attacks in Crimea Deprive Towns of Power and Water
